title: Renewal Propensity Signal Crosswalk & Action Grid (working template)
body:
Purpose:
This is a working crosswalk to translate raw product + commercial signals into a single renewal propensity score and a compact action grid for CS reps. Meant for QBR prep and weekly renewal prioritization.

Scope / audience:
- Audience: AEs + CSMs + CS Ops.
- Scope: 30–90 day renewal horizon (primary), also usable for mid-cycle escalation.
- Not intended to replace bespoke enterprise playbooks (those stay in customer-level runbooks).

Quick notes (working):
- Keep signals simple and sourceable from Snowflake/BI. If a metric is noisy, mark as FLAG and validate.
- Default window is 90 days for behavioral signals unless otherwise noted.
- We want a score that is human-interpretable (0–100) and maps to three actionable buckets.

Signal definitions (candidate list):
1) Usage depth (core-product monthly active seats / active users):
   - Metric: 30d active users / paid seats (or seats touched). Window: 30d.
   - Rationale: adoption inside account. Lower ratio -> weaker usage.
   - Measurement: percent (0–100).

2) API request trend:
   - Metric: % change in daily API calls (7d avg) vs prior 30d baseline. Window: 7d trend.
   - Rationale: sudden drop is early warning.

3) Feature adoption (key features used):
   - Metric: count of new-feature events (e.g., batching, caching enabled, custom prompts) in 90d.
   - Rationale: signal of technical maturity.

4) Support ticket cadence / severity:
   - Metric: tickets opened in 30d weighted by severity (P0=3, P1=2, P2=1).
   - Rationale: operational pain correlates with churn.

5) Billing signal (spend trend / overdue invoices):
   - Metric: month-over-month billed consumption growth; overdue invoice flag.
   - Rationale: cost friction or contraction.

6) Performance incidents / latency SLO breaches:
   - Metric: number of infra incidents affecting account in 90d.
   - Rationale: reliability impact.

7) Model quality regressions (evals):
   - Metric: drop in key eval prompt-set pass rate > X% in 30d.
   - Rationale: product output quality affects user trust.

8) Customer engagement signals:
   - Metric: last logged-in date, number of account-owner meetings in 90d, response rate to CS outreach.

9) NPS / CSAT trend (if available):
   - Metric: delta vs previous quarter.

Scoring approach (simple, transparent):
- Each signal is normalized to a 0–100 subscore (higher = better).
- Assign weights (preliminary) summing to 100. Weights in parentheses below.

Weights (starter):
- Usage depth (25)
- API request trend (15)
- Feature adoption (12)
- Support tickets (10)
- Billing signal (12)
- Performance incidents (10)
- Model quality (8)
- Engagement (6)
- NPS/CSAT (2)

Scoring buckets for each signal (example):
- Usage depth: >70% -> 100, 40–70% -> 60, 10–40% -> 30, <10% -> 0
- API trend: rising >10% ->100, flat (-10..10)->60, falling -10..-40->30, <-40->0
- Support tickets: 0 tickets ->100, 1 low-sev ->80, 1 high-sev or 3 low-sev ->40, recurring high-sev ->0
- Billing: growth >10% ->100, flat ->70, slight contraction ->40, overdue/stop-pay ->0
(Full signal buckets to be codified in CS Ops workbook.)

Calculation (example):
1) Compute normalized subscores per signal (0–100).
2) Multiply subscores by weights, sum, divide by 100 to get final score (0–100).
3) Round to nearest integer.

Example calculation (toy account):
- Usage depth: 55% -> subscore 60 * weight 25 = 1500
- API trend: -20% -> subscore 30 * weight 15 = 450
- Feature adoption: moderate -> subscore 60 * weight 12 = 720
- Support: 1 P1 in 30d -> subscore 40 * weight 10 = 400
- Billing: flat -> subscore 70 * weight 12 = 840
- Performance: 0 incidents -> 100 * 10 = 1000
- Model quality: slight dip -> 80 * 8 = 640
- Engagement: 1 meeting -> 80 * 6 = 480
- NPS: no data -> default 60 * 2 = 120
Sum = 5650 / 100 = 56.5 -> Score = 57 ("At-risk" bucket).

Risk buckets + recommended cadence / playbook (action grid):
- High risk (score 0–35):
  Actions: immediate CS + AE joint outreach (aim to convert to survival plan), technical deep-dive w/ SRE & Applied ML, 1-week SLA on major fixes, escalate to customer exec sponsor, consider discount/contract amendment only if remediation plan exists.
  Cadence: daily check-ins until remediated, weekly updates to Customer Success Director.

- At-risk (36–60):
  Actions: schedule tactical QBR within 10 business days, prioritize engineering triage for P1 items, introduce usage nudges (playbooks), demo advanced features, discuss pricing alignment and short-term incentives.
  Cadence: weekly outreach; biweekly QBR if needed.

- Healthy (61–100):
  Actions: standard QBR cadence (quarterly), explore expansion opportunities, ensure exec sponsorship is engaged for renewals, monitor for regressions.
  Cadence: monthly health check, quarterly business review.

Signal quality flags (meta):
- FLAG - usage depth suspect if seat metadata missing (CS Ops data quality ticket).
- FLAG - model quality requires linked eval set; if missing -> default conservative subscores.
- FLAG - billing anomalies should be double-checked with finance before outreach.

Operational notes / data sources (who to call):
- Product telemetry / Snowflake: events.product.*, metrics.usage_daily (owner: Data/BI)
- Billing: billing.invoices / finance ledger (owner: Finance Ops)
- Support tickets: Zendesk/Intercom export (owner: Support)
- Incidents: PagerDuty/Statuspage JSON (owner: SRE)
- NPS: SurveyMonkey / Delighted exports (owner: CS Ops)

Implementation checklist (short):
- [ ] Create Snowflake views to normalize signals (JIRA-4521).
- [ ] Add a Snowplow event for "feature_opt_in" (product PR required).
- [ ] Add data-quality monitor for seats mapping (alert to CS Ops).
- [ ] Ship a first-pass Looker dashboard for weekly renewal queue.
- [ ] Pilot with 15 accounts for 30 days, gather feedback.

QBR integration (how CS should use):
- At QBR prep, pull final score + top-3 negative signals and include as first slide ("Renewal health snapshot").
- CSMs should author 1-line risk hypothesis and 3 prioritized asks (engineering, finance, executive).
- Use the action grid to tag required stakeholders and timeline.

Example slide bullet (copyable):
- Renewal snapshot: Score 57 (At-risk) — primary drivers: API drop (-20%), new-feature adoption low. CS ask: engineering triage for elevated error rate + AE to review pricing elasticity.

Open questions / discussion items (to resolve in pilot):
- Should NPS be weighted higher for enterprise vs SMB? (proposal: split weight profiles by segment).
- How to treat accounts with seasonal usage? Add smoothing or seasonality flags.
- Contractual constraints: how to reflect multi-year/auto-renew clauses?
- Ownership: who is final approver for automated escalation? (CS Director?)

Notes to self / TODOs: 
- Capture edge-case examples (large-but-sparse usage accounts).
- Build a one-page cheat sheet for reps (playbook quick reference).
- Plan internal brown-bag to get buy-in from AE org (target: 2025-03-15).

Appendix: quick reference mapping (for engineers)
- Snowflake view names: cs_signals.usage_summary_90d, cs_signals.api_trends_7d, cs_signals.feature_counts_90d, cs_signals.ticket_summary_30d
- Alerts to create: cs_alerts.overdue_invoice, cs_alerts.api_drop_30pct, cs_alerts.incident_count_high

End of working template.

(Internal — rough draft; expect revisions after pilot and CS Ops validation.)
